# jslet — Developer Tools & Engineering Calculators
> Free client-side developer tools (JSON, regex, Base64, timestamps, CSS) and engineering calculators (cloud cost, GPU, Kubernetes, SRE).
> All tools run entirely in-browser with zero data collection. No signup, no tracking, no server-side processing.

## Site Map

### Core Pages
- [Home](https://www.jslet.com/): 138 free developer tools and engineering calculators — 52+ JS dev tools, 77+ cloud calculators, all client-side, zero tracking.
- [About & Contact](https://www.jslet.com/about): Mission, team, and contact channels.
- [Privacy](https://www.jslet.com/privacy): Privacy policy.
- [Terms](https://www.jslet.com/terms): Terms of service.
- [RSS Feed](https://www.jslet.com/rss.xml): jslet Intel Briefings RSS.

### 🟢 JS Developer Tools (NEW)

- [Password & API Key Generator](https://www.jslet.com/password-generator): Generate cryptographically secure passwords, passphrases, and API keys entirely in-browser with a live strength meter. Exclude-lookalikes, per-type guarantees, batch mode, custom key prefixes. Web Crypto API entropy, zero network traffic.
- [Favicon Generator](https://www.jslet.com/favicon-generator): Generate a full favicon package from emoji, text or color — 16/32/180/192/512 PNGs, manifest.json with maskable icon, HTML code. Canvas-drawn, zero upload.
- [PX to REM Converter](https://www.jslet.com/px-to-rem): Convert px to rem, em and percent with a configurable root font size (default 16px). Bulk mode converts an entire stylesheet preserving comments. Breakpoint reference table.
- [CSS Animation Generator](https://www.jslet.com/css-animation-generator): Visually design CSS keyframe animations with live preview — 12 compositor-safe presets, duration/easing/delay/iteration/direction/fill-mode controls. Copy-ready CSS.
- [Flexbox Generator](https://www.jslet.com/flexbox-generator): Visually design CSS Flexbox layouts with live preview — direction, wrap, justify/align, gap, per-item flex-grow/shrink/basis and presets. Copy-ready CSS.
- [CSS Grid Generator](https://www.jslet.com/css-grid-generator): Visually design CSS Grid layouts with live preview — columns, rows, gaps, alignment, custom templates, fr/minmax/auto-fit patterns and presets. Instant copy-ready CSS.
- [HTTP Status Codes](https://www.jslet.com/http-status-codes): Complete reference for all 63 standard HTTP status codes with meanings, real-world causes, and fixes. Searchable and filterable by class. 100% client-side.
- [XML Formatter & Validator](https://www.jslet.com/xml-formatter): Beautify, minify and validate XML with native DOMParser line/column error reports, 3 indent styles, and XML↔JSON conversion.
- [Case Converter](https://www.jslet.com/case-converter): Convert text between six naming conventions in real time — camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, kebab-case, Title Case. Acronym and number-aware word tokenizer. 100% client-side.
- [JSON Tools](https://www.jslet.com/json-tools): JSON formatter, validator, CSV converter, diff checker, minifier, JSON-to-code generator.
- [Regex Tools](https://www.jslet.com/regex-tools): Regex tester with real-time matching, visualizer, cheatsheet, and regex replace tool.
- [Encoding Tools](https://www.jslet.com/encoding-tools): Base64 encode/decode (text + images), URL encode/decode, JWT decoder, HTML entities, Unicode escape.
- [Timestamp Tools](https://www.jslet.com/timestamp-tools): Unix epoch converter, ISO 8601 formatter, timezone converter, date diff, batch timestamp converter.
- [CSS & Color Tools](https://www.jslet.com/css-tools): Hex→RGB→HSL converter, CSS gradient editor, box shadow generator, CSS unit converter, color palette generator.
- [More Dev Tools](https://www.jslet.com/dev-tools): cURL→Fetch converter, HTML→JSX, Markdown preview, UUID generator, character/byte counter, MIME type lookup.
- [CSV to JSON Converter](https://www.jslet.com/csv-to-json): Convert CSV to JSON with RFC 4180 parsing, BOM stripping, type-inference switch and 4 output formats. 100% client-side.
- [JSON Formatter](https://www.jslet.com/json-formatter): Format and validate JSON with syntax highlighting and line numbers. Auto-fixes trailing commas. 100% client-side.
- [Base64 Encode / Decode](https://www.jslet.com/base64-encode-decode): Encode text, files, and images to Base64. Drag-and-drop image support.
- [JWT Decoder](https://www.jslet.com/jwt-decoder): Decode JWT header, payload, and signature. Auto-detects expiry without secret key.
- [Unix Timestamp Converter](https://www.jslet.com/unix-timestamp-converter): Convert Unix epoch to human dates and back. Live UTC clock.
- [Color Converter](https://www.jslet.com/color-converter): Convert between hex, RGB, RGBA, HSL, HSLA. Click-to-copy CSS values.
- [HTML to Markdown Converter](https://www.jslet.com/html-to-markdown): Convert HTML fragments to GitHub-flavored Markdown — headings, tables, code, links, images, lists, blockquotes, with HTML fallback for inexpressible constructs.
- [Text to Slug Generator](https://www.jslet.com/text-to-slug): Convert titles to SEO-friendly URL slugs — English and Chinese (pinyin option), configurable separator, batch mode, 60-char truncation check.
- [User Agent Parser](https://www.jslet.com/user-agent-parser): Parse User-Agent strings — browser, version, OS, device, engine, and crawler detection with the matching rules shown.
- [cURL to Fetch Converter](https://www.jslet.com/curl-to-fetch): Convert cURL commands to JavaScript fetch(), axios, or got code.
- [Regex Tester](https://www.jslet.com/regex-tester): Real-time regex matching with capture group highlighting. Supports g/i/m/s/u flags.

### Tech-Intel Briefing (38 articles)

- [The Error Budget: 99.9% Is 43.2 Minutes. Most Teams Never Spend a Second of It.](https://www.jslet.com/error-budget-real): An error budget is a decision mechanism, not a metric. Covers burn-rate alerting (14.4x/1h, 6x/6h, 1x/3d), the SLO-vs-SLA gap that creates the safety margin, and a graduated freeze policy (50% review / 75% sign-off / 100% freeze). A 30-minute outage consumes 69% of a 99.9% monthly budget; 99.99% leaves 4.3 minutes. Companion to the Error Budget calculator and The Price of a Nine.
- [The AZ Tax](https://www.jslet.com/cross-az-tax-real): Cross-AZ transfer bills $0.01/GB in each direction and never appears as a line item — it hides inside EC2-Other and ELB usage types. Four architectures priced with 2026 rates: a 10K rps 3-tier app = $5,013/mo, chatty microservices = $6,266/mo, a 1K rps API = $501/mo, cross-region replicas = $300/mo. Complete free/paid boundary map (same-AZ public-IP trap, RDS Multi-AZ exemption), NAT Gateway stacking math, AZ-affinity decision logic, 5-step audit checklist. Companion to the Cross-AZ Cost Calculator.
- [The Base64 Inflation: The 33% Tax on Every JWT, Data URI, and API Payload](https://www.jslet.com/base64-inflation-tax-real): Base64 inflation measured on real payloads: 10-byte secret +60%, 32-byte JWT key +37.5%, 200KB screenshot → 267KB data URI. The 33% figure is the floor, not the rule. The compression trap: gzip after base64 is 22% worse than gzip alone. Includes data-URI break-even analysis, decision framework, 5-step audit checklist. Companion to The Bundle Tax and The Image Weight Tax.
- [The Bundle Tax: Why Your 2 MB JavaScript Bundle Costs Users 300ms](https://www.jslet.com/bundle-tax-real): 1 MB JS = 30ms parse on desktop, 90-150ms on mid-range phone. Gzip saves 85% of transmission, Brotli 95%, but parsing runs on the full uncompressed source. JSON.parse is 10-20x faster than JS object literals for data. Includes mobile multiplier, zone-based decision framework, 5-step migration checklist. Companion to The Image Weight Tax.
- [The Animation Tax: Why Animating Width Costs 273ms of Layout Per 1.8 Seconds](https://www.jslet.com/animation-tax-real): Measured Chrome tracing — a 3,000-element width animation triggers 110 layout passes (273ms + 213ms paint) in 1.8s; the identical transform animation triggers zero. The compositor rule, fill-mode/replay/will-change traps, decision framework, 5-step audit. Companion to The Layout Tax.
- [The Layout Tax: Why Your 10,000-Element Grid Costs Users 8ms Per Frame](https://www.jslet.com/layout-tax-real): Measured Chrome benchmarks on CSS layout cost — a 10K-element grid reflows in 7.9ms (47% of a frame budget, 2x block layout), layout scales superlinearly, and read-write interleaving (thrash) costs 101x more than batched writes. Includes the three layout taxes, mobile multiplier, content-visibility guidance, decision framework, 5-step audit. Companion to The Bundle Tax and The Image Weight Tax.
- [The XML Tax](https://www.jslet.com/xml-tax-real): Measured — XML costs 46% more bytes than JSON and parses 2.6x slower on identical data; the attribute-vs-element rewrite saves 81%. Why XML survives (XSD, namespaces) and when to convert. Companion to The JSON.parse Tax.
- [The JSON.parse Tax](https://www.jslet.com/json-parse-tax-real): Measured Chrome benchmarks on JSON.parse — memory double-billing (object tree = 138% of input, peak ~2.4x the file), the reviver callback trap (11.9x slowdown for a no-op), and the first-byte tax (NDJSON shows first data 100x faster on slow networks). Decision framework, 5-step audit. Companion to The Bundle Tax and the frontend performance-tax series.
- [The Image Weight Tax: Why Your WebP Migration Cuts Your CDN Bill in Half](https://www.jslet.com/image-weight-tax-real): Images are 50-70% of page weight. We measured 3,000 images: WebP q75 is 80% smaller than JPG q75 and 97% smaller than PNG; lossless WebP beats PNG by 90% on UI screenshots. At 50K pageviews/month, format migration removes ~300 GB egress — half a CDN bill. Includes bandwidth math, JPG generation-loss trap, 2026 format decision framework, 5-step migration checklist.
- [UUID v4 vs v7: Why Random Primary Keys Destroy Write Performance](https://www.jslet.com/uuid-v4-vs-v7-real): v4 scatters writes across B-tree pages. v7 puts a 48-bit millisecond timestamp first. 73% fewer page splits, 40% more INSERTs/sec, 18% smaller indexes. Collision math unchanged. Storage engine behavior transformed.
- [The Observability Tax: Why Your Logs Cost More Than Your Servers](https://www.jslet.com/observability-cost-real): Observability = 15-25% of cloud spend. Datadog custom metric cardinality: one tag with 1,000 values = $100/month. Splunk ingest: 93% of data never queried. Trace head-sampling: blind to P99. Self-hosted Grafana (Loki+Mimir+Tempo) is 53% cheaper at 200 hosts, 69% at 500. Breakeven at ~70-100 hosts.
- [The Bitrate Ladder Racket: Why Your 1080p Stream Uses 4K Bandwidth](https://www.jslet.com/streaming-bandwidth-real): VBR encoding peaks at 2× nominal. HLS overhead +15%. Live vs VOD are fundamentally different formulas. Ads + DVR + multi-CDN multiply bandwidth. H.264→H.265 saves 40% at 10× encoding cost; AV1 saves 50% vs H.264 at 20× encoding cost.
- [The Tail Latency Trap: Why Your P99 Budget Says 200ms and Users Experience 2 Seconds](https://www.jslet.com/latency-budget-real): Fan-out tail amplification — 10 backends × P99=50ms = composite P99 120-180ms. Protocol stack tax (3 RTTs before first byte). Serialization overhead (JSON vs Protobuf at 10 hops). Queueing delay (80% utilization = 40% latency increase from queueing). Physics floor (NY→London = 56ms RTT).
- [The OOMKill Reaper: Why Your Kubernetes Pods Die at 2 AM](https://www.jslet.com/container-resource-limit-real): JVM RSS = Xmx × 2.2 (heap + Metaspace + threads + JIT + malloc). Request=limit wastes 43% cluster capacity. CFS throttling creates self-amplifying P99 spikes. Runtime memory models for JVM, Go (1.5×), Node.js (1.8×). VPA-based decision framework.
- [The Rate Limit Racket: Why Your API Gateway Costs 30× More Than Self-Hosted](https://www.jslet.com/api-rate-limit-cost-real): Per-request pricing is the decoy. Data transfer, throttling retry amplification, and multi-region fragmentation are the real cost drivers. gRPC saves 40% bandwidth. Self-hosted NGINX on $132/month reserved instances = 98% cheaper at 5,000 rps. Breakeven at ~500 rps.
- [The Serverless Tax: Why Your Lambda Function at $8.50/Month Actually Costs $427](https://www.jslet.com/lambda-cost-real): Lambda's pricing page shows $0.0000166667/GB-second. Real production functions cost 10-50× more. Five structural taxes: VPC cold starts, provisioned concurrency premiums, CloudWatch Logs inflation (surpasses compute within 90 days), cross-AZ egress to RDS/ElastiCache, and Step Functions orchestration costing 12.5× the Lambdas. Includes Lambda vs EC2 vs Fargate breakeven at steady throughput.
- [The Reservation Trap: Why Your 3-Year RI Is a $200K Bet Against AWS Spot Pricing](https://www.jslet.com/ri-vs-spot-breakeven-real): A 3-year Standard RI is not a discount — it's a 36-month cash advance to AWS. The breakeven depends on one variable: spot interruption rate. A 1% move flips a $200K commitment from savings to loss. Deconstructs the breakeven surface, Convertible RI liquidity premium for GPU instances, Savings Plan structural arbitrage in heterogeneous fleets, cross-region spot diversification economics, and the three-tier mixed-fleet allocation framework (base = RI, burst = spot, buffer = on-demand).
- [The NAT Gateway Trap: Why Your Private Subnet Costs $450/Month Before It Serves a Single User](https://www.jslet.com/nat-gateway-cost-real): Each NAT Gateway costs $32.85/mo per AZ idle. 3 AZs = $98.55 before a byte. Data processing at $0.045/GB. Cross-AZ traffic double-counted at $0.02/GB. Three real bill walkthroughs. VPC Endpoint arbitrage: S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints free, ECR/CloudWatch Interface Endpoints 78% cheaper on data. EC2 NAT instance 10× cheaper. Terraform/CDK default trap explained.
- [Kafka Partitions: The Hidden RAM Tax](https://www.jslet.com/kafka-partitions-ram-tax): Every Kafka partition costs ~0.50 MB of broker heap before a single message. At scale, partition metadata consumes 50% of broker RAM. Five structural limits beyond RAM: file descriptor exhaustion, shutdown time, G1GC degradation, batching collapse, controller overload. Three real broker deaths. Practical partition budget framework.
- [CDN Cache Hit Ratio: Why 95% Is Still Costing You Money](https://www.jslet.com/cdn-cache-hit-ratio-real): The miss-ratio math that changes CDN economics. Going 95→9% hit ratio isn't a 4% improvement — it's an 80% reduction in origin traffic. Deconstructs 6 structural leaks: TTL misconfiguration, Vary-header fragmentation, query string noise, cookie-based bypass, AI crawler uniqueness, and invalidation cascades. Origin shield economics. Byte hit vs. request hit ratio. Three real CDN bill walkthroughs and a TTL engineering framework.
- [LLM Inference Latency: Why Your 7B Model Gets 15 tok/s on a T4 but 3,500 tok/s on an H100](https://www.jslet.com/llm-inference-latency): Memory bandwidth is the real bottleneck — not TFLOPS. Model throughput across 12 models × 7 GPUs × 4 quantization levels, with real benchmark data from Llama, Mistral, and DeepSeek deployments.
- [DNS Propagation Time: Resolver-by-Resolver Timing Model](https://www.jslet.com/dns-propagation): DNS propagation isn't one number — it's a distribution shaped by TTL, ISP resolver caching policy, and geographic anycast topology. Interactive calculator with 8 resolver populations modeled.
- [Token Economics: Why Your LLM Bill Is 3× What the Pricing Page Promised](https://www.jslet.com/llm-api-pricing-real): Five structural leaks between LLM pricing pages and real costs. Self-hosted vs API breakeven math across model scales. Provider-by-provider breakdown for 12 models.
- [Connections ≥Concurrency: Why Your Database Connection Pool Is Too Big](https://www.jslet.com/database-connection-pool-real): Every ORM ships with a connection pool default of 100. The PostgreSQL wiki recommends 17 on an 8-core NVMe server. The 83-connection gap is a throughput penalty. Includes PgBouncer decision framework.
- [Cloud Storage Costs: The Egress Trap — Why Your $/GB Number Is Lying to You](https://www.jslet.com/cloud-storage-cost-real): S3 Standard costs $0.023/GB. R2 costs $0.015/GB with zero egress. At 10 TB stored and 50 TB served, R2 is $150/mo and S3 is $4,730/mo — a 31× gap. Full 6-vendor comparison.
- [Kubernetes Pod Density: Why 110 Pods Is a Lie](https://www.jslet.com/pod-density-real): K8s says 110 pods per node. Your CNI says 40. The four binding constraints modeled across EKS, GKE, and AKS — with DaemonSet tax and bin packing math.
- [UUID v4 Collision Probability at Scale](https://www.jslet.com/uuid-v4-collision-probability-real): 2.71 quintillion UUIDs for a 50% collision chance. The math says never. Every documented production collision traces to a bad entropy source.
- [RAID 5 vs RAID 6: 20TB Rebuild Times Compared](https://www.jslet.com/raid-5-vs-raid-6-rebuild-ure): RAID 6 rebuild is only 13% slower than RAID 5. The URE survival gap is five orders of magnitude. Stop comparing the wrong number.
- [Password Crack Times: The Algorithm Gap — Your Hash Function Matters More Than Your Password Length](https://www.jslet.com/password-crack-time-real): bcrypt cost 12 on an 8-char password: ~3 years on an RTX 4090. SHA-256 unsalted on the same password: less than a second. The hash algorithm gap is 5 million to 1.
- [99.9% vs 99.99% vs 99.999%: How Much Does Each Extra 9 Cost?](https://www.jslet.com/system-availability-sla-economics): 99.9% uptime = 8.76 hours downtime/year. 99.999% = 5 minutes 15 seconds. Going from 3 to 5 nines costs roughly 4× more in infrastructure and 8× more in engineering time. Breakeven economics.
- [GPU Training Costs: The arXiv-to-Bill Gap](https://www.jslet.com/gpu-training-cost-real): The paper says 72 GPU-hours on 8×A100. Your cloud bill says 90. Five structural leaks: utilization loss, Xid errors, hyperparameter search, checkpoint storage, and cross-cloud egress.
- [RAID 5 Is Dead: Why 12TB+ Drives Make Single Parity Mathematically Unsafe](https://www.jslet.com/raid-5-is-dead): At 12 TB per drive, a RAID 5 rebuild faces 99.9% failure probability from URE alone. The math broke somewhere around 2019. RAID 6 or erasure coding is the minimum viable parity.
- [VPN Protocol Overhead Encyclopedia: WireGuard, IPsec, OpenVPN](https://www.jslet.com/vpn-overhead-encyclopedia): Measured per-packet overhead for WireGuard, IPsec, OpenVPN, GRE, SSTP. TCP-over-TCP problem, MTU optimization, protocol ranking by use case.
- [The Price of Observability: Why Your Monitoring Bill Exceeds Your Infrastructure Bill](https://www.jslet.com/observability-cost): Observability consumes 15–25% of total cloud spend. Datadog at 200 hosts: $36,270/month. Self-built LGTM: $4,900/month. Same telemetry, 86% less. Five solutions modeled across three scales.
- [The Managed Database Cost Illusion: Why "Same PostgreSQL" Costs 2× More on RDS Than Aurora](https://www.jslet.com/rds-cost-real): RDS doubles compute on Multi-AZ. io1 IOPS can cost 19× more than storage. RDS is the only provider that charges for retained backups — Aurora, Cloud SQL, and Azure DB don't. Four workload scenarios modeled across all four providers with 2026 list prices.
- [The LCU Trap: Why Your Load Balancer Bill Has Nothing To Do With Bandwidth](https://www.jslet.com/alb-nlb-cost-real): ALB and NLB bill by LCU — you pay for the MAX dimension, not the sum. NLB handles 32× more new connections per LCU. ALB rule evaluations can silently become the binding dimension at 50+ rules. Five workload profiles modeled across both load balancer types.
- [AWS Egress vs DigitalOcean: Real Cost Comparison](https://www.jslet.com/aws-egress-vs-digitalocean): Nobody benchmarks egress — until the bill arrives. AWS charges up to $0.09/GB. DigitalOcean includes 11 TB of free egress per Droplet. Three workload scenarios priced through both models.
- [The Post-Human Web: AI Agent Traffic Eclipses Human Traffic Vectors](https://www.jslet.com/post-human-web-inversion): For the first time in internet history, bots outnumber humans online — 53% of all web traffic is automated. AI crawler traffic grew 300% YoY. Quantifies infrastructure cost impact on CDN egress and origin servers.

## 🗃️Decision Matrix Tools
